newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Barito soars 12.90 pct on rumours.
newsitem.headline: Barito soars 12.90 pct on rumours.

text.p: Shares of Indonesia's timber conglomerate PT Barito Pacific Timber Group made sharp gains in late trading on Monday on acquisition rumours, brokers said.
Barito topped the active list as it rose 12.90 percent, or 200 rupiah, to 1,750 rupiah, on a volume of more than 20 million shares.
"Barito stole market attention on rumours Mbak Tutut plans to buy a large stake in Barito," one broker with a local brokerage firm said.
President Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hadiyanti Rukmana, popularly known as Mbak Tutut, controls toll-road builder and operator PT Citra Marga Nusaphala Persada.
A Barito official declined to comment on the rumours but said the market had possibly started to realise the value of the stock.
Another broker, however, said the rise was due to market talk of expected strong earnings in 1996 after reports of a rise in Indonesia's forestry exports last year.
Indonesia's export earnings from the forestry sector rose to $8.3 billion in 1996 from $7.1 billion in 1995.
